candidates.explanation: The design clearly provides a framework-neutral operation, capability-shaped provider port, dedicated abort-aware SSE Route Handler, resettable idle timeout, pre/post-commit failure handling, channel-native job decisions, shared failure/reporting primitives, and provider-safe contracts. Colocation is partial because assistant behavior is dispersed across global domain, ports, use-cases, boundary, adapter, and infrastructure roots.

The proposal correctly separates a transport-neutral generation use case and provider port from dedicated SSE and job adapters. It covers abort propagation, idle rather than total timeout, commit-aware failure representation, exactly-once reporting, safe failure normalization, and appropriate retry/dead-letter behavior. Colocation is partial because the capability is spread across global architectural directories rather than one assistant root.

Assistant policy, contracts, provider adaptation, streaming support, and reporting are coherently grouped under the capability, with justified framework and job entry surfaces. The design uses a framework-neutral operation and provider seam, preserves abort and iterator cleanup, implements a resettable idle watchdog, distinguishes pre-commit HTTP errors from post-commit SSE failures, keeps job semantics native, and prevents provider details from leaking.

The proposal presents a cohesive assistant module with narrow client, stream, and job surfaces plus the required App Router endpoint. It clearly defines a framework-neutral generation operation and provider-independent port, propagates cancellation, enforces per-token idle timing without a total deadline, handles failures according to commit state, shares semantic classification/reporting while retaining native channel contracts, and protects provider details and server-only imports.
